newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-POLISH NBP SINKS ZLOTY, SPARKS CAPITAL INFLOW.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-POLISH NBP SINKS ZLOTY, SPARKS CAPITAL INFLOW.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland on Thursday pounded the zloty down to its lowest level in 10-weeks with repeated currency-buying interventions, triggering a wave of foreign capital inflows into Polish paper, dealers said.

They said foreign investors, who over the last several weeks bought small amounts of T-bills during a period of relative zloty strength, flooded into Polish treasuries as the zloty tumbled 0.8 point against the basket on Thursday.

"The NBP was determined to knock the zloty down today despite foreign investor inflows, which eventually created zloty support around 2.5 percent from the parity rate," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

The zloty closed at 2.54/2.46 percent from the trading band centre, down from Wednesday's close at 3.24/3.21 percent after the central bank drained nearly $200 million from the market between 3.2 and 2.4 percent from the parity rate.
It closed at 3.1460/80 to the dollar, down nearly three figures from yesterday's 3.1200/10 and at 1.8215/35 to the mark, against Wednesday's close at 1.8082/87.

Dealers said the central bank would likely keep the zloty anchored around present levels against the currency basket for the next few weeks, but said that in the longer term the NBP would be forced to intervene to cap zloty gains again.

"Foreign direct investment and portfolio inflows are likely to push the zloty higher after a period of stabilisation around 2.5 percent from parity," said Karol Zaluski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

Dealers said, however, that the central bank, which often said it did not want speculative foregin capital inflows into Polish treasuries, may be reluctant to let the zloty go back toward three percent and give foreigners an attractive profit.
The central bank declined to comment on its currency-buying operations on Thursday.
Howerver, dealers said that today's foreign inflows may help the Polish Treasury by increasing demand at Monday's 1.3 billion zloty primary auction and pulling down yields.
"It is time to buy T-bills, but yields may take a beating on Monday because of the large amount of foreign bids," said one dealer at a large Polish bank.
Dealers said foreign investors quickly bought all available treasuries on Poland's shallow secondary market on Thursday, focusing on 52-week bills, last yielding 21.93 percent.
Foreigners were attracted to Polish T-bills after yields increased more than two percentage points in the first three months of 1997 before hitting a ceiling in early April.
